stage: 1b — seed replication of the two near-miss candidates
question: are the two smallest Stage-1 retain-same shortfalls stable across independent training seeds, or one draw?

why_this_study_exists.stage1_result: all eight B4 replay candidates disqualified; B0 selected; the Stage-2 gate opened
why_this_study_exists.what_stage1_could_not_decide: the floor is a point comparison over one training seed, so a shortfall of 3 queries and a shortfall of 59 are the same kind of verdict
why_this_study_exists.post_hoc_check_that_shaped_this_design: re-scoring the same eight candidates against a more lenient MG anchor also rejects all eight, so the binding limitation is the measurement, not the choice of anchor

parents.selection_rule: the two candidates whose retain-same row-micro shortfall against B0 is smallest when expressed in QUERIES, taken from the filed Stage-1 report
parents.not_selected_on: D_G. Selecting the two best on the criterion would be selecting on the outcome being revisited

seeds.why_reused: its adapter and predictions were produced and scored by Stage 1; re-running the same seed would produce a second draw from an identical RNG state and say nothing about between-seed variance
seeds.why_these: the three integers after the recipe default, fixed here before training so they cannot be chosen after seeing results

consumed_at: random.Random(f"{recipe.seed}:{epoch}:{gi}").shuffle(order) — the per-group per-epoch order of the interleaved stream
what_a_seed_varies.does_not_vary: which examples are trained on, so the fit/probe partition is untouched by replication
what_a_seed_varies.reachability_asserted_at_runtime: the trainer raises unless ReferenceRecipe(**overrides).seed equals the replicate's seed

primary_rule.statement: for each of the four frozen numbers, the MEAN over replicates must be at or above the Stage-1 B0 anchor
primary_rule.why_unrounded: rounding the mean to the four decimals its inputs carry would let a rounding step decide a comparison the inputs did not

rejected_alternative.status: rejected in Stage 1 and not reintroduced here
rejected_alternative.why: it is not a resolvable gap, not an interval width and not a pre-registered effect size

reported_but_not_decision_bearing.why_not_an_interval: with k=4 an interval imports a distributional assumption the design does not need; the observed range answers whether every independent seed fell below the anchor
reported_but_not_decision_bearing.distance_to_mg: reported per replicate and as a mean; the floor decides eligibility, exactly as in Stage 1

anchor.why_a_point: B0 is the no-op copy of MF and takes zero training steps, so it has no seed variance; the determinism control below is what tests whether it has generation variance

generation_determinism_control.what_it_does: regenerates B0 into this study's own predictions directory under the Stage-1 contract and compares it row by row with Stage 1's B0 parquet
generation_determinism_control.stops_the_study_if: any of the four floor numbers moves
generation_determinism_control.why: a point floor over a non-reproducible anchor is not interpretable and replication cannot repair it

already_measured_from_two_existing_parce.comparison: identical B0 adapter bytes generated under image_batch_size 8 (pilot-100) and 1 (Stage 1)
already_measured_from_two_existing_parce.why_zero: the floor's 408 + 76 probe queries are 100% text_to_text; every flip is image-route
already_measured_from_two_existing_parce.consequence_for_d_g: generation noise of order 2e-4, ~17x smaller than the gap between Stage 1's two best candidates (0.027343 vs 0.030686), so it does not reorder them — but D_G's sixth decimal is not physically meaningful, and the frozen tie-break compares at exactly six decimals
already_measured_from_two_existing_parce.what_it_cannot_show: whether generation is deterministic under a FIXED contract, which is the assumption every replicate comparison rests on — hence the control

generation_contract.why_a_separate_directory: the control regenerates B0, so this study needs a file called predictions_tv_B0.parquet. In Stage 1's directory that name is already taken by filed evidence whose sidecar carries a different experiment_id, so the sidecar would refuse reuse and REGENERATE OVER IT. A separate directory makes that impossible rather than unlikely — the same reasoning Stage 1 recorded for not using the pilot-100 directory

refusal_policy.reason: a replication protocol written after its replicates were trained could be fitted to them, which is the one thing a replication is supposed to make impossible

limitations: Replication does not increase the query count. The probe half is 35 entities / 408 retain-same and 23 donors / 76 retain-other queries, fixed by the association pool, so retain-other stays resolvable only in units of 1/76 = 0.0132 however many seeds are run.
k=4 per parent. A mean over four draws bounds training-seed variance loosely and licenses no interval claim.
Two parents only. This says nothing about the other six Stage-1 candidates.
The probe half carries 1 of the 6 taxonomic retained associations, so taxonomic retention remains unmeasured, as in Stage 1.
Exploratory: no hypothesis is tested and no error rate is controlled. A pass is a reason to design a confirmatory protocol, not a claim.

rule.why_entity_not_association: An association-level split leaves a probe fact belonging to an entity whose other facts were rehearsed, so the entity was partly seen.  Entity-level makes 'never replayed' true of a whole entity's knowledge.
rule.cut: first half of the ordering is PROBE, remainder is FIT

amendments.reason: Added the guarded --refreeze/--reason amendment path to this script after the initial freeze; the script hashes itself, so the amendment records the change instead of leaving the freeze stale.

Added the LPT lane planner to the trainer, removed an unused import and an unused local from the analyzer, replaced a hardcoded seed literal with BASE_SEED, and sorted the import block. All three are protocol paths, so the freeze re-binds them; no criterion value, seed, parent or rule changed.

Fixed a real defect the tests caught: the analyzer read the Stage-1 generation contract through a non-existent attribute (fisr.STAGE1_FREEZE instead of the imported STAGE1_FREEZE_REPORT), which would have raised AttributeError at run time in enforce_contract. Also made the trainer tolerate only the frozen validator's grid-structural B0 error, with a guard that stops if that message ever changes, and factored the determinism control's decision into compare_floor_numbers so it is testable without a parquet. No seed, parent, rule, epsilon or contract value changed.

Fixed a real path defect the first run exposed after two seconds: control_b0 built its Stage-1 predictions path as repo_root/'data'/dataset_dir_for_tag('iter12'), but dataset_dir_for_tag already returns a data/-prefixed path, so it opened data/data/mllmu_hier_pilot100/... and raised FileNotFoundError after the chain had claimed a GPU. Every path this study touches now resolves through five helpers in seed_replication.py, used by both the analyzer and the trainer, with tests pinning the trap (dataset_dir_for_tag starts with data/) and asserting no helper emits a double prefix. No seed, parent, rule, epsilon, contract or anchor value changed.
